question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the signed flux

$$
\Phi=\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S
$$

for the vector field

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\langle x,2 y,- 2 z - 2\rangle.
$$

The parametric surface is

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle u,v,u v\rangle.
$$

Use the parameter rectangle

$$
-1\le u\le 0,\qquad 1\le v\le 3.
$$

Use the orientation induced by $\mathbf r_v\times\mathbf r_u$. Enter an exact value.

$\Phi=$ {{flux}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the parametric flux formula with the specified orientation:

$$
\Phi=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv.
$$

Differentiate the parametrization:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=\langle 1,0,v\rangle \\ \mathbf r_v&=\langle 0,1,u\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Compute the cross product:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k \\ 1&0&v \\ 0&1&u\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\langle - v,- u,1\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Reverse its sign for the specified order:

$$
\mathbf N=-\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\langle v,u,-1\rangle.
$$

Substitute the surface coordinates into the field:

$$
x=u,\quad y=v,\quad z=u v.
$$

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\langle u,2 v,- 2 u v - 2\rangle.
$$

Form the three signed dot-product contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1}&=(u)(v) \\ &=u v \\ T_{2}&=(2 v)(u) \\ &=2 u v \\ T_{3}&=(- 2 u v - 2)(-1) \\ &=2 u v+2\end{aligned}
$$

Collect the polynomial terms, writing $g(u,v)=T_1+T_2+T_3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(u,v)&=5 u v+2\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive with respect to $v$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(u,v)&=\frac{5 u v^{2}}{2}+2 v\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both inner endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=\int_{1}^{3}g(u,v)\,\mathrm dv \\ &=\left[P(u,v)\right]_{v=1}^{v=3}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=20 u+4\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive of $H(u)$ with respect to $u$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(u)&=10 u^{2}+4 u\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both outer endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}\Phi&=\int_{-1}^{0}H(u)\,\mathrm du \\ &=\left[Q(u)\right]_{u=-1}^{u=0} \\ &=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

The cross product includes the surface area scale; there is no extra normalization factor.

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the signed flux

$$
\Phi=\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S
$$

for the vector field

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\langle 1 - x,2 y,2 z + 2\rangle.
$$

The parametric surface is

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle u + v,u - v,u v\rangle.
$$

Use the parameter rectangle

$$
0\le u\le 1,\qquad 1\le v\le 3.
$$

Use the orientation induced by $\mathbf r_v\times\mathbf r_u$. Enter an exact value.

$\Phi=$ {{flux}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the parametric flux formula with the specified orientation:

$$
\Phi=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv.
$$

Differentiate the parametrization:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=\langle 1,1,v\rangle \\ \mathbf r_v&=\langle 1,-1,u\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Compute the cross product:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k \\ 1&1&v \\ 1&-1&u\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\langle u + v,- u + v,-2\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Reverse its sign for the specified order:

$$
\mathbf N=-\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\langle - u - v,u - v,2\rangle.
$$

Substitute the surface coordinates into the field:

$$
x=u + v,\quad y=u - v,\quad z=u v.
$$

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\langle - u - v + 1,2 u - 2 v,2 u v + 2\rangle.
$$

Form the three signed dot-product contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1}&=(- u - v + 1)(- u - v) \\ &=u^{2}+2 u v \\ &\quad {}- u+v^{2} \\ &\quad {}- v \\ T_{2}&=(2 u - 2 v)(u - v) \\ &=2 u^{2}- 4 u v \\ &\quad {}+2 v^{2} \\ T_{3}&=(2 u v + 2)(2) \\ &=4 u v+4\end{aligned}
$$

Collect the polynomial terms, writing $g(u,v)=T_1+T_2+T_3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(u,v)&=3 u^{2}+2 u v \\ &\quad {}- u+3 v^{2} \\ &\quad {}- v+4\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive with respect to $v$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(u,v)&=3 u^{2} v+u v^{2} \\ &\quad {}- u v+v^{3} \\ &\quad {}- \frac{v^{2}}{2}+4 v\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both inner endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=\int_{1}^{3}g(u,v)\,\mathrm dv \\ &=\left[P(u,v)\right]_{v=1}^{v=3}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=6 u^{2}+6 u \\ &\quad {}+30\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive of $H(u)$ with respect to $u$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(u)&=2 u^{3}+3 u^{2} \\ &\quad {}+30 u\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both outer endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}\Phi&=\int_{0}^{1}H(u)\,\mathrm du \\ &=\left[Q(u)\right]_{u=0}^{u=1} \\ &=35.\end{aligned}
$$

The cross product includes the surface area scale; there is no extra normalization factor.

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the signed flux

$$
\Phi=\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S
$$

for the vector field

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\langle - 2 x - 2,- y,- 2 z - 1\rangle.
$$

The parametric surface is

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle u v,u,v\rangle.
$$

Use the parameter rectangle

$$
1\le u\le 3,\qquad -1\le v\le 1.
$$

Use the orientation induced by $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$. Enter an exact value.

$\Phi=$ {{flux}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the parametric flux formula with the specified orientation:

$$
\Phi=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv.
$$

Differentiate the parametrization:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=\langle v,1,0\rangle \\ \mathbf r_v&=\langle u,0,1\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Compute the cross product:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k \\ v&1&0 \\ u&0&1\end{vmatrix} \\ &=\langle 1,- v,- u\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $\mathbf N=\langle 1,- v,- u\rangle$.

Substitute the surface coordinates into the field:

$$
x=u v,\quad y=u,\quad z=v.
$$

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\langle - 2 u v - 2,- u,- 2 v - 1\rangle.
$$

Form the three signed dot-product contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1}&=(- 2 u v - 2)(1) \\ &=- 2 u v-2 \\ T_{2}&=(- u)(- v) \\ &=u v \\ T_{3}&=(- 2 v - 1)(- u) \\ &=2 u v+u\end{aligned}
$$

Collect the polynomial terms, writing $g(u,v)=T_1+T_2+T_3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(u,v)&=u v+u \\ &\quad {}-2\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive with respect to $v$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(u,v)&=\frac{u v^{2}}{2}+u v \\ &\quad {}- 2 v\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both inner endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=\int_{-1}^{1}g(u,v)\,\mathrm dv \\ &=\left[P(u,v)\right]_{v=-1}^{v=1}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=2 u-4\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive of $H(u)$ with respect to $u$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(u)&=u^{2}- 4 u\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both outer endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}\Phi&=\int_{1}^{3}H(u)\,\mathrm du \\ &=\left[Q(u)\right]_{u=1}^{u=3} \\ &=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The cross product includes the surface area scale; there is no extra normalization factor.
